sources: dossier=Net position L9 declares the shape `holds: { <alias>: { from: <upstream-type> } }` but is silent on whether the key must match the upstream's declared claim alias vs an arbitrary local name; design corpus=claim-handle.md L56/L75 confirm co-holder rows are declared via `holds:` but likewise don't state the key-matching rule; test=lib/graph/node/template_validator_holds_test.go (TestValidateHolds_Ok, TestValidateHolds_UnknownClaimAlias) proves the map key is validated against the upstream node's declared claim alias, erroring `holds_unknown_claim_alias` on mismatch; code=template_validator_holds.go:15-48 validates the key (not `binding.As`) against the upstream's claims: block, runner_locks.go:167-170 applies `binding.As` as a separate local rename applied only at substitution time.
note: No dossier or design-corpus statement covers this template-grammar detail, but two purpose-built validator tests unambiguously establish the intended shape (key = upstream's declared alias; `As` is a separate optional local rename), satisfying the tests tier of the intent-source precedence. The doc's 'entries each name a local alias' claim was backwards and omitted the rename field entirely. Rewrote the template-shape sentence to state the key names the upstream's declared alias and mention the optional local rename.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors L27 'Poison rule with forward propagation' (2026-06-21, 10cf843b, transcript): 'when any holder fails, every participating holder is driven to failed via auto_terminal_abandon at the resolution moment'; design corpus=cancel-siblings.md Definition ('A property on the strict aggregation policy... Declared on the fan-out parent's error policy') and auto-terminal.md Invariants (poison rule is the co-holder failure mechanism); doc=claim-co-holdership.md:32 said 'The default cancel-siblings error policy walks the co-holder set when one fails'; code=lib/graph/node/template_validator_holds.go:137-141 (cancel_siblings rejected outside error_policy.kind=strict) and lib/runtime/run_tree.go:99 (`if policy.CancelSiblings`, opt-in) corroborate.
note: Dossier transcript entry establishes the actual co-holder-failure mechanism (poison rule via auto-terminal), directly contradicting the doc's claim that a 'default cancel-siblings' policy walks co-holders. cancel-siblings.md (design corpus, adjacent concept) independently confirms cancel-siblings is opt-in and walks fan-out sub-claims, not co-holders. Rewrote the line to describe the poison rule and explicitly distinguish it from cancel-siblings.

sources: dossier=Intentional absences L37: the verifier-executor pattern is 'deliberately documentation plus binaries, NOT a rimsky concept or template-language sugar' (2026-05-15, artifact); repo rule=.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md self-containment rule disallows references to external documentation in concept bodies; doc=claim-co-holdership.md:24 Boundaries 'Does NOT own: ...the verifier pattern documentation'.
note: The dossier confirms the verifier-executor pattern is deliberately outside the concept catalog, but the Boundaries line cites it as unresolvable external documentation, which the design corpus's own self-containment rule forbids and which resolves to nothing for a reader (no slug, no location). Dropped the dangling disclaimer from the Does NOT own list; the substantive boundary (claim acquisition, parent-run aggregation) is unaffected.

sources: dossier=silent on the term 'cell graph'; design corpus=grep for 'cell graph' across .ok-planner/design/ hits only claim-co-holdership.md:28; catalog defines `concept:graph` ('rimsky's unit of node connectivity... Templates declare one or more graphs') and `concept:cascade-graph` (an unrelated operator-dashboard concept), no cell-graph artifact; doc=claim-co-holdership.md:28 'a subset of the cell graph'.
note: No concept named or aliased 'cell graph' exists in the catalog; the co-holdership `from:` edges are edges within the template's declared graph (`concept:graph`). Rewrote to cite `concept:graph` by slug instead of the undefined term.

sources: dossier=Net position L13 ('Co-held claims ride the executor wire identically to acquired claims — a leaf executor cannot tell the difference') and Required behaviors L19 (2026-05-15 plan; 2026-06-10 cascade-and-claim-handoff artifact: 'the executor cannot distinguish acquired from co-held... the same acquired result the original acquirer received'); doc=claim-co-holdership.md:29 'same wire shape as a fresh acquire' — matches the dossier's stated intent; code=runner_dispatch.go makeHeldClaimHandle (925-948) sets only alias/address/payload while makeClaimHandle (950-979) also sets Kind, intent, and CandidateHandle.
note: The dossier independently (Net position + Required behaviors, cross-corroborated) mandates full wire-shape parity such that an executor cannot distinguish acquired from co-held claims. The doc correctly states this intent. The finding's code evidence (Kind/intent/CandidateHandle left unset on co-held handles) is accurate and shows code has drifted from the dossier-established intent — this is a code defect, not a doc defect. Doc left unchanged; queuing fix-code only, per instructions not to touch code.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors L23 'Auto-terminal premature-firing guard' (2026-05-15, plan notes, artifact): resolution 'refuses to fire while an expected member has not yet inserted its row' unless any-failed; design corpus=auto-terminal.md What-it-is ('waits until every expected holding-subgraph member has inserted its holder row and, for handles with expected fan-out children, until every child has resolved'); doc=claim-co-holdership.md:31 said auto-terminal 'fires when every co-holder row... is non-active' (sufficiency) vs Definition L11's correct 'fires only after' (necessity); code=auto_terminal.go:55-63 (expectedInheritorsMissing gate), :77-81 (children-count gate).
note: Dossier artifact entry plus the adjacent auto-terminal.md concept doc both confirm additional necessary gates beyond all-rows-non-active (expected-member presence, fan-out children resolution) that the Invariants line's 'fires when' (sufficiency) framing omitted, contradicting the doc's own correct Definition-section phrasing. Reworded to 'fires only after' and deferred the full gate list to concept:auto-terminal's ownership.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors L27 'Poison rule with forward propagation' (2026-06-21, 10cf843b, transcript); design corpus=cancel-siblings.md (named Adjacent to claim-co-holdership in its own Boundaries) Definition + Multi-supervisor scope section confirm cancel-siblings is opt-in, walks the fan-out parent's sibling sub-claims, and cancel-siblings.md L11 already correctly says 'parent's other in-flight sub-claims'; doc=claim-co-holdership.md:32 said 'default cancel-siblings error policy walks the co-holder set'; code=aggregation_policy.go:30-40 (CancelSiblings defaults false, rejected outside kind=strict), terminal_decision_cancel.go:42-45 (walks ListChildClaimHandles, claim-tree children, not co-holders), runner_terminal_release.go:140 (FailAllActiveByClaimHandle is the actual co-holder-failure path).
note: Same underlying doc line and defect as row 28 (duplicate finding on the same sentence); ruling and fix applied together. Adjacent concept cancel-siblings.md's own Definition and Multi-supervisor scope section directly contradict claim-co-holdership.md's characterization, and the dossier's transcript-tier poison-rule entry names the real mechanism. Fix already applied under row 28's edit.
